questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution outlines the principle of just and humane conditions of work?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 42**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 42** of the Indian Constitution directs the State to ensure the provision of just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief.
 
• This article is part of the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**, which are non-justiciable but serve as guiding principles for governance.
 
• It emphasizes the responsibility of the State to improve labor conditions and promote social justice.
 
• The provision aims to protect workers' rights and promote welfare measures, particularly for women workers and marginalized laborers.
 
• It serves as a basis for labor laws and welfare schemes aimed at improving workplace conditions and maternity benefits in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP):**

 
 
• Part IV (Articles 36–51) of the Indian Constitution contains the DPSPs, which are guidelines for the State to ensure socio-economic justice.
 
• They are not enforceable by courts but are fundamental in policymaking and governance.
 
 
 
• **Labor Welfare in India:**
 
 
• India has implemented various labor laws, such as the Factories Act, 1948, and the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, to ensure humane working conditions and maternity relief.
 
• These laws are influenced by the principles enshrined in Article 42.
 
 
 
• **Social Justice:**
 
 
• Article 42 promotes social justice by advocating for equitable working conditions and support for vulnerable workers.
 
• It aligns with global labor standards set by institutions like the International Labour Organization (ILO).
 
 
 
• **Maternity Relief:**
 
 
• Article 42 specifically mentions maternity relief, emphasizing the need for paid leave and health benefits for women workers.
 
• The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017, which provides 26 weeks of paid maternity leave, is a significant step in this direction.

questions.question: Which Ummathat folk dancer was awarded the Padma Shri in March 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rani Machaiah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Rani Machaiah**, a renowned Ummathat folk dancer from Karnataka, was conferred with the prestigious **Padma Shri** in March 2023.
 
• The Ummathat dance is a traditional folk dance performed by the Kodava community of Karnataka, and Rani Machaiah has been a significant contributor to preserving and promoting this art form.
 
• She was recognized for her exceptional efforts in **reviving, teaching, and popularizing the Ummathat dance** both within India and internationally.
 
• The Padma Shri award, one of the highest civilian honors in India, was presented to her for her contributions to **Art** in the traditional folk category.
 
• Her work has not only highlighted the cultural heritage of the Kodava community but also inspired younger generations to embrace their traditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Padma Shri Award**

 
 
• It is the fourth highest civilian award in India, instituted in 1954.
 
• The award recognizes distinguished contributions in various fields, including Art, Literature, Education, Science, Sports, Medicine, Social Work, Public Affairs, and more.
 
• Recipients are announced annually on the eve of Republic Day.
 
 
 
• **Ummathat Dance**
 
 
• It is a traditional folk dance performed exclusively by women of the Kodava community in Karnataka.
 
• The performers wear traditional Kodava attire and adorn themselves with jewelry while dancing to rhythmic drumbeats.
 
• The dance is usually performed during festivals, weddings, and other cultural celebrations.
 
 
 
• **Kodava Community**
 
 
• The Kodavas are an ethnolinguistic group native to the Kodagu district in Karnataka, India.
 
• They have a rich cultural heritage, known for their unique customs, traditional attire, and martial history.
 
• Their cultural practices include folk dances like Ummathat and traditional festivals such as Kailpodh and Puthari.
 
 
 
• **Folk Dance in India**
 
 
• India is known for its diverse folk dances, which represent the traditions and heritage of various communities across the country.
 
• Examples include Garba from Gujarat, Bihu from Assam, Ghoomar from Rajasthan, and Lavani from Maharashtra.
 
• Folk dances play a vital role in preserving India's cultural diversity and are often performed during festivals and social gatherings.

questions.question: Which industry is involved in the extraction of raw materials from nature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Extractive industry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The extractive industry is primarily involved in the **extraction of natural resources** such as minerals, ores, oil, natural gas, and other raw materials directly from the Earth.
 
• This industry includes activities such as **mining, quarrying, oil and gas extraction, and forestry**.
 
• It plays a vital role in providing **raw materials** required for various industries like manufacturing, construction, and energy production.
 
• Examples of extractive industry operations include **coal mining, crude oil drilling, and metal ore extraction**.
 
• The extractive industry is regulated globally to minimize its **environmental and social impact**, as it often involves disruption to ecosystems and local communities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Primary Sector:**

 
 
• The extractive industry is a part of the **primary sector**, which includes industries that use natural resources directly.
 
• Other primary sector activities include agriculture, fishing, forestry, and animal husbandry.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact:**
 
 
• The extractive industry can lead to **deforestation, habitat destruction, pollution, and depletion of non-renewable resources**.
 
• Countries and organizations are increasingly promoting **sustainable extraction practices** to mitigate these effects.
 
 
 
• **Economic Importance:**
 
 
• Natural resource extraction contributes significantly to a country's **GDP and employment**, particularly in resource-rich nations.
 
• For example, oil and gas extraction is a major contributor to the economies of countries like Saudi Arabia, Russia, and the United States.
 
 
 
• **Technological Advancements:**
 
 
• Technological innovations, such as **automated mining equipment and advanced drilling techniques**, have improved efficiency and safety in the extractive industry.
 
• However, these advancements also raise concerns about **job displacement** and the need for workforce reskilling.
 
 
 
• **Legal and Ethical Considerations:**
 
 
• Many countries have established regulations to ensure **fair labor practices and environmental compliance** in the extractive industry.
 
• Global initiatives like the **Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI)** aim to promote accountability and reduce corruption in resource extraction.

questions.question: A pyranometer is a ______ measuring instrument, commonly used for climate research or monitoring weather performance.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**solar irradiance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A pyranometer is an instrument used to measure **solar irradiance**, which refers to the power of solar radiation per unit area.
 
• It measures both **direct and diffuse solar radiation** from the hemisphere above it.
 
• Pyranometers are essential tools in **climate research**, solar energy monitoring, and meteorological studies.
 
• They are commonly used to evaluate the performance of solar panels and track weather patterns.
 
• The instrument typically works by using a thermopile sensor to convert the heat from solar radiation into an electrical signal, which is then measured.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solar Irradiance:**

 
 
• It is the amount of solar power received per unit area, expressed in watts per square meter (W/m²).
 
• It plays a critical role in understanding Earth's climate system and energy balance.
 
• There are three types of solar irradiance: **global horizontal irradiance (GHI)**, **direct normal irradiance (DNI)**, and **diffuse horizontal irradiance (DHI)**.
 
 
 
• **Working Principle of Pyranometers:**
 
 
• The device uses sensors like thermopiles or photovoltaic cells to detect solar radiation.
 
• A glass dome protects the sensor and ensures a wide field of view while minimizing external interference.
 
• The output is usually in the form of a voltage signal proportional to the solar irradiance.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Pyranometers:**
 
 
• Used in **solar power plants** to monitor and optimize energy production.
 
• Deployed in **meteorological stations** for weather forecasting and climate studies.
 
• Utilized in building design for **energy efficiency** analysis.
 
 
 
• **Calibration and Standards:**
 
 
• Pyranometers are calibrated against a reference instrument under standard test conditions.
 
• The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) provides guidelines for pyranometer accuracy and usage.

questions.question: Which of the following classical dances uses the ‘pung’ as the most important instrument?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manipuri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Manipuri** is a classical dance form originating from the northeastern state of Manipur, India.
 
• The **'pung'**, a traditional drum, is the most important instrument used in Manipuri dance performances.
 
• The pung is integral to Manipuri dance as it provides rhythmic beats and sets the pace for the dancers.
 
• Manipuri dance is characterized by graceful and fluid movements, often depicting themes from **Vaishnavism** and episodes from the **life of Lord Krishna.**
 
• The dance form is deeply rooted in the cultural traditions of Manipur and is performed during religious and cultural occasions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Classical Dance Forms of India**

 
 
• India has eight classical dance forms recognized by the Sangeet Natak Akademi: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Odissi, and Sattriya.
 
• Each dance form is deeply intertwined with the cultural and religious heritage of its region of origin.
 
• These dances often depict stories from Indian epics like the Mahabharata and Ramayana.
 
 
 
• **Role of Instruments in Classical Dance**
 
 
• Instruments like the pung, mridangam, tabla, veena, and flute play a pivotal role in classical dance performances.
 
• They provide rhythm, melody, and emotional depth, enhancing the overall appeal of the dance.
 
 
 
• **Manipuri Dance Features**
 
 
• Manipuri is known for its **circular and seamless movements**, soft hand gestures, and spiritual essence.
 
• Costumes are elaborate, including vibrant saris and unique accessories that add to the visual appeal.
 
 
 
• **Vaishnavism Influence**
 
 
• Manipuri dance often portrays themes from **Vaishnavism**, focusing on devotion to Lord Krishna and Radha.
 
• It is performed during festivals like **Rasa Lila**, showcasing episodes from Krishna's life.

questions.question: In which of the following countries does the Brahmaputra River NOT flow?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nepal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Brahmaputra River originates from the **Angsi Glacier in the Tibet Autonomous Region of China** and flows through China, India, and Bangladesh.
 
• In China, the river is known as the **Yarlung Tsangpo**, where it flows eastward through the Tibetan Plateau.
 
• In India, the river enters through the state of Arunachal Pradesh, where it is called the **Siang or Dihang River**, and later merges with tributaries to become the Brahmaputra.
 
• In Bangladesh, the river is known as the **Jamuna River**, eventually merging with the Ganges (Padma) before flowing into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• **Nepal does not lie in the path of the Brahmaputra River**, as the river flows to the east of Nepal's territory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brahmaputra River Basin**

 
 
• The Brahmaputra River Basin spans multiple countries: **China, India, and Bangladesh**.
 
• The basin covers an area of approximately **580,000 square kilometers**.
 
• It is one of the largest river systems in the world and is highly significant for agriculture, hydropower, and biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Significance**
 
 
• The Brahmaputra is known for its strong and unpredictable currents, making it one of the most dynamic rivers in the world.
 
• It forms one of the world's largest riverine islands, **Majuli**, in Assam, India.
 
• The river's delta, formed with the Ganges, is the largest delta in the world, known as the **Sundarbans Delta**.
 
 
 
• **Economic Importance**
 
 
• The river supports millions of people through agriculture, fishing, and transportation.
 
• It is a critical source of freshwater and hydroelectric power, with several dams and projects planned along its course.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Importance**
 
 
• The Brahmaputra River supports a rich biodiversity, including species like the endangered Gangetic dolphin and the one-horned rhinoceros.
 
• The river's floodplains are ecologically sensitive and host a variety of flora and fauna.

questions.question: What was the role of the prime minister in the planning commission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ex-Officio chairman**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Prime Minister of India served as the **Ex-Officio Chairman** of the Planning Commission during its existence (1950–2014).
 
• The Planning Commission was an institution in the Government of India that formulated India’s Five-Year Plans and various economic policies.
 
• The role of the Ex-Officio Chairman was to provide strategic direction and oversee the formulation and execution of national plans.
 
• The Prime Minister, as the Ex-Officio Chairman, held ultimate authority in decision-making within the Planning Commission.
 
• In 2015, the Planning Commission was replaced by the NITI Aayog, and the Prime Minister became the Ex-Officio Chairman of the NITI Aayog as well.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Planning Commission**

 
 
• Established in 1950 by a resolution of the Government of India under the chairmanship of Jawaharlal Nehru.
 
• The body was tasked with assessing resources and drafting Five-Year Plans to achieve economic and social goals.
 
• It functioned as an advisory body to the Government of India.
 
• It was dissolved in 2014 and replaced by the NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India).
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog**
 
 
• Formed on January 1, 2015, as the successor to the Planning Commission.
 
• Aims to foster cooperative federalism by involving states in the policy-making process.
 
• Focuses on long-term policy planning and innovation to achieve sustainable development goals.
 
• The Prime Minister serves as the Ex-Officio Chairman of NITI Aayog, with a Governing Council comprising Chief Ministers of states and Union Territories.
 
 
 
• **Five-Year Plans**
 
 
• These were centralized and integrated national economic programs.
 
• India implemented 12 Five-Year Plans between 1951 and 2017.
 
• The first Five-Year Plan focused on agriculture, while later plans emphasized industrialization, infrastructure, and economic liberalization.
 
• After the dissolution of the Planning Commission, Five-Year Plans were replaced by long-term strategies under NITI Aayog.
 
 
 
• **Ex-Officio Position**
 
 
• The term "Ex-Officio" refers to a position held by someone by virtue of another office or role they hold.
 
• For example, the Prime Minister automatically became the Ex-Officio Chairman of the Planning Commission and now of NITI Aayog.
 
• This ensures that the highest executive authority is directly involved in strategic planning and decision-making.

questions.question: Dalchand Sharma is an eminent Pakhawaj exponent of which of the following gharanas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nathdwara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dalchand Sharma is a renowned exponent of the **Pakhawaj**, a traditional Indian percussion instrument.
 
• He is associated with the **Nathdwara Gharana**, which is famous for its tradition of Pakhawaj playing.
 
• The Nathdwara Gharana has its roots in the temple town of Nathdwara in Rajasthan and is deeply influenced by the **Vaishnavite devotional music traditions.**
 
• Dalchand Sharma has contributed significantly to preserving and popularizing the Pakhawaj through performances and teaching.
 
• The **Pakhawaj** is a barrel-shaped drum that is primarily used in Hindustani classical music and accompanies genres like **Dhrupad**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pakhawaj**

 
 
• The Pakhawaj is a traditional Indian percussion instrument, known for its deep, resonant sound.
 
• It is an ancient drum that predates the tabla and is closely associated with the **Dhrupad** style of Hindustani classical music.
 
• The Pakhawaj is played using both hands, with specific strokes producing distinct tones on either side of the drum.
 
• Its construction involves a wooden barrel body with leather drum heads on both sides, tuned using leather straps.
 
 
 
• **Nathdwara Gharana**
 
 
• This gharana is named after the temple town of Nathdwara in Rajasthan.
 
• It is known for its association with the **devotional music of the Pushtimarg sect**, dedicated to Lord Krishna.
 
• Artists of this gharana specialize in Pakhawaj playing and maintain a rich tradition of rhythmic compositions.
 
 
 
• **Dhrupad**
 
 
• Dhrupad is one of the oldest genres of Hindustani classical music, emphasizing spiritual and meditative aspects.
 
• It is characterized by slow, deliberate movements and the use of the Pakhawaj for rhythmic accompaniment.
 
• This style is often performed in temples and has a strong connection to India's cultural heritage.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Gharanas in Music**
 
 
• A gharana represents a specific school or style of classical music, passed down through generations.
 
• Each gharana is unique in its approach to melody, rhythm, and technique.
 
• Gharanas play a crucial role in preserving the diversity and richness of Indian classical music traditions.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Treaty of Bassein signed between the British East India Company and Baji Rao II, the Maratha Peshwa?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1802**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Treaty of Bassein was signed on **31 December 1802** between the British East India Company and Baji Rao II, the Maratha Peshwa.
 
• It was a significant event that marked the beginning of British dominance over the Maratha Confederacy.
 
• Under the treaty, Baji Rao II accepted the subsidiary alliance system, agreeing to maintain a **British military force** within his territory in exchange for protection.
 
• The treaty led to the Second Anglo-Maratha War (1803–1805), as other Maratha leaders opposed the agreement and British interference.
 
• This treaty ultimately weakened the Maratha Empire and paved the way for British expansion in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subsidiary Alliance:**

 
 
• A diplomatic strategy introduced by Lord Wellesley in 1798 to establish British dominance in India.
 
• Under this system, Indian rulers were required to accept a British military presence and pay for its maintenance, losing their autonomy in foreign affairs.
 
• The Treaty of Bassein was a classic example of the subsidiary alliance system.
 
 
 
• **Second Anglo-Maratha War (1803–1805):**
 
 
• It was triggered by the Treaty of Bassein as other Maratha leaders, such as Scindia and Bhonsle, opposed British control.
 
• The British emerged victorious, significantly reducing Maratha power and influence.
 
 
 
• **Baji Rao II:**
 
 
• He was the last formal Peshwa of the Maratha Empire.
 
• His tenure was marked by internal Maratha conflicts and increasing British intervention.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Treaty:**
 
 
• The treaty marked a turning point, as it weakened the Marathas and strengthened British control over India.
 
• It set the stage for further conflicts, eventually leading to the complete dissolution of the Maratha Empire by 1818.

questions.question: Two objects A and B of mass 2 kg and 3 kg, respectively, were dropped from different heights. A took 5 second and B took 3 seconds to touch the ground. What is the ratio of their kinetic energy with which they hit the ground?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**50/27**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The kinetic energy of an object is given by the formula: **KE = 1/2 mv²**, where m is the mass and v is the velocity of the object.
 
• When objects are dropped from a height, their final velocity (v) upon hitting the ground can be calculated using the equation of motion: **v = g × t**, where g is the acceleration due to gravity (9.8 m/s²) and t is the time taken to reach the ground.
 
• For object A (mass = 2 kg, time = 5 s): vA = g × t = 9.8 × 5 = 49 m/s. KEA = (1/2) × 2 × (49)² = 2401 J.
 
• For object B (mass = 3 kg, time = 3 s): vB = g × t = 9.8 × 3 = 29.4 m/s. KEB = (1/2) × 3 × (29.4)² = 1294.38 J.
 
• The ratio of their kinetic energies: KEA : KEB = 2401 : 1294.38 ≈ **50 : 27**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kinetic Energy:** The energy possessed by a body due to its motion. It is directly proportional to the mass of the object and the square of its velocity.
 
• **Equation of Motion:** The equation v = g × t assumes free-fall conditions where air resistance is negligible, and the object starts from rest.
 
• **Acceleration due to Gravity (g):** The rate at which an object accelerates when in free fall near the Earth's surface, typically 9.8 m/s².
 
• **Relationship between Mass and Kinetic Energy:** Kinetic energy depends linearly on mass; hence, a heavier object has higher kinetic energy if velocity remains constant.
 
• **Practical Implications:** This principle is widely applied in mechanics, aerospace, sports physics, and other fields where motion and energy analysis are crucial.

questions.question: Garib Kalyan Rojgar Yojana was launched in 2020 by the Government of India to provide work for ___________ days.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**125 days**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Garib Kalyan Rojgar Yojana** was launched by the Government of India in 2020 to address the challenges faced by migrant workers during the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• It aims to provide **employment opportunities for 125 days** in 116 districts across six states in India.
 
• The scheme covers areas such as **construction, rural infrastructure, sanitation, and agricultural activities** to ensure livelihood generation.
 
• It focuses on utilizing resources under various government programs like MNREGA, PMAY, and rural schemes.
 
• The target beneficiaries of the scheme are **returnee migrant workers** affected by the economic slowdown due to the pandemic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MNREGA):**

 
 
• A flagship scheme of the Government of India aimed at providing at least 100 days of wage employment to rural households.
 
• It plays a pivotal role in generating rural livelihood and empowering women and marginalized communities.
 
• MNREGA funding is utilized in Garib Kalyan Rojgar Yojana to create employment opportunities.
 
 
 
• **PM Garib Kalyan Package:**
 
 
• An economic relief package announced in March 2020 to support poor and vulnerable sections during the COVID-19 crisis.
 
• It included direct cash transfers, free food grains distribution, and support for healthcare workers.
 
• The employment initiative under Garib Kalyan Rojgar Yojana complements this package.
 
 
 
• **Rural Infrastructure Development:**
 
 
• Key focus areas include rural road construction, water conservation, waste management, and housing development.
 
• Such projects under Garib Kalyan Rojgar Yojana aim to boost rural employment and improve living standards.
 
 
 
• **COVID-19 and Migrant Workers:**
 
 
• The pandemic led to unprecedented challenges for migrant workers, including loss of jobs and reverse migration.
 
• Garib Kalyan Rojgar Yojana was specifically designed to address these challenges by providing livelihood opportunities in their native districts.

questions.question: Which of the following Union Ministries introduced the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Amendment Bill, 2024, in the Parliament in February 2024?

options.text: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Amendment Bill, 2024, was introduced by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change** in February 2024.
 
• The amendment aims to strengthen existing laws related to the **prevention and control of water pollution** and enhance accountability mechanisms.
 
• The bill proposes to update penalties and compliance measures for industries and entities found violating pollution norms.
 
• The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change oversees policies and programs aimed at **environmental conservation, pollution mitigation, and climate change adaptation**.
 
• The amendment is aligned with India's commitment to achieving **sustainable development goals (SDGs)**, particularly SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974:**

 
 
• The original act was enacted to prevent and control water pollution and maintain or restore the wholesomeness of water in India.
 
• It led to the establishment of **Central and State Pollution Control Boards** for monitoring and enforcement.
 
• The act provides the framework for regulating industries and other entities that discharge waste into water bodies.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goal 6 (SDG 6):**
 
 
• SDG 6 aims to ensure availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all.
 
• It emphasizes targets such as improving water quality, reducing pollution, and increasing water-use efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change:**
 
 
• The ministry is responsible for planning, promoting, coordinating, and overseeing the implementation of environmental and forestry programs.
 
• It plays a key role in formulating policies aimed at environmental protection and sustainable development.
 
 
 
• **Water pollution:**
 
 
• Water pollution refers to contamination of water bodies such as lakes, rivers, oceans, and groundwater.
 
• Major causes include industrial discharge, agricultural runoff, and untreated sewage.

questions.question: In June 2024, Yusuf Pathan, a former cricketer, won the Lok Sabha seat in Baharampur; which state was this constituency located in?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**West Bengal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Baharampur is a Lok Sabha constituency located in the **Murshidabad district** of West Bengal.
 
• West Bengal has **42 Lok Sabha constituencies**, making it one of the states with significant representation in the Parliament.
 
• The region of Baharampur is historically known for its **role during the Bengal Renaissance** and has a rich cultural and political legacy.
 
• Murshidabad, where Baharampur is located, was once the capital of Bengal during the Mughal period.
 
• The constituency has been represented by various prominent leaders in Indian politics over the years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lok Sabha Constituencies:**

 
 
• India has a total of **543 Lok Sabha constituencies**, each representing a specific geographical area.
 
• The Lok Sabha is the **lower house of Parliament**, and members are directly elected by citizens of India.
 
• West Bengal contributes **42 seats** to the Lok Sabha, which is among the highest in India.
 
 
 
• **Murshidabad District:**
 
 
• Murshidabad is known for its historical significance as the **former capital of Bengal**.
 
• The district is famous for landmarks such as **Hazarduari Palace** and the **Katra Mosque**.
 
• It is culturally rich and has played a pivotal role in Bengal’s history.
 
 
 
• **Bengal Renaissance:**
 
 
• The Bengal Renaissance was a cultural, social, and political movement during the 19th and early 20th centuries.
 
• It marked a period of significant reform and progress in Bengal, impacting education, literature, and politics.
 
 
 
• **West Bengal Politics:**
 
 
• West Bengal has been a key player in Indian politics, with significant contributions from leaders like **Rabindranath Tagore, Subhas Chandra Bose**, and others.
 
• Political parties like the **Trinamool Congress (TMC)** and **Communist Party of India (CPI)** have historically dominated the state.

questions.question: Which organic leavener is used in the baking industry to make bread, pastries and cakes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Yeasts**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Yeasts** are single-celled fungi widely used as a natural leavening agent in baking.
 
• They convert sugars into carbon dioxide and ethanol through the process of **fermentation**, causing dough to rise.
 
• Commonly used yeast species in baking include **Saccharomyces cerevisiae**.
 
• Yeasts are essential in making bread, pastries, and cakes as they improve texture, flavor, and volume.
 
• They are also used in other industries, such as brewing and bioethanol production.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fermentation:**

 
 
• A metabolic process where microorganisms like yeast convert carbohydrates into alcohol or acids.
 
• In baking, fermentation produces carbon dioxide, which causes dough to expand and rise.
 
 
 
• **Saccharomyces cerevisiae:**
 
 
• Commonly known as baker's yeast, it is a species of yeast used in baking, brewing, and winemaking.
 
• It is known for its efficiency in sugar fermentation and its ability to produce high-quality products.
 
 
 
• **Leavening agents:**
 
 
• Substances used in baking to produce gas and expand dough or batter.
 
• Types include biological (yeast), chemical (baking powder and soda), and physical (air and steam).
 
 
 
• **Role of yeast in baking:**
 
 
• Yeast fermentation enhances the flavor of baked goods by producing secondary metabolites.
 
• It contributes to the light, airy texture of bread and other baked goods.

questions.question: During which period were coal mines nationalised in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1971-1975**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The nationalization of coal mines in India occurred during the period **1971-1975**.
 
• The process began with the **nationalization of coking coal mines** through the Coking Coal Mines (Emergency Provisions) Act, 1971.
 
• In **1973**, the Coal Mines (Nationalization) Act was passed, extending nationalization to non-coking coal mines.
 
• The nationalization aimed to regulate coal production, improve safety measures, and ensure equitable distribution of coal resources.
 
• The nationalized coal mines were brought under the control of public sector companies like **Coal India Limited (CIL)** and its subsidiaries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Coal India Limited (CIL)**

 
 
• CIL is a public sector company established in **1975** and is headquartered in Kolkata, India.
 
• It is the largest coal-producing company in the world and operates under the Ministry of Coal.
 
• CIL is responsible for meeting the growing energy demands of India through coal production.
 
 
 
• **Types of Coal**
 
 
• Coal is classified into different types based on carbon content: **Anthracite, Bituminous, Sub-bituminous, and Lignite**.
 
• Coking coal is used in steel production, while non-coking coal is primarily used for electricity generation.
 
 
 
• **Reasons for Nationalization**
 
 
• The coal industry faced challenges such as unscientific mining practices, poor safety standards, and exploitation of labor.
 
• Nationalization aimed to address these issues and ensure efficient use of coal resources for national development.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Nationalization**
 
 
• It led to the creation of a structured and organized coal industry in India.
 
• Nationalization improved safety measures, working conditions, and production efficiency.
 
• It enabled the government to control coal prices and ensure equitable distribution.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT responsible for investigating complaints of violations of human rights in India?

options.text: National Human Rights Commission of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**International Human Rights Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **International Human Rights Commission (IHRC)** is a global organization and does not have jurisdiction to investigate human rights violations within India.
 
• Human rights complaints in India are primarily handled by national statutory bodies like the **National Human Rights Commission of India (NHRC)**.
 
• Other commissions, such as the **National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC)** and the **National Commission for Women (NCW)**, investigate rights violations specific to their respective domains in India.
 
• The IHRC is focused on international advocacy and awareness rather than direct investigation or enforcement of human rights laws in individual countries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Human Rights Commission of India (NHRC):**

 
 
• Established in 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, the NHRC is a statutory body in India.
 
• It investigates complaints of human rights violations and recommends remedial action to the government.
 
• The commission also promotes research and awareness about human rights issues in India.
 
 
 
• **National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC):**
 
 
• Constituted under Article 338 of the Indian Constitution, the NCSC safeguards the rights of Scheduled Castes in India.
 
• It monitors the implementation of constitutional and legal safeguards for Scheduled Castes and investigates related complaints.
 
 
 
• **National Commission for Women (NCW):**
 
 
• Set up in January 1992, the NCW focuses on protecting and promoting the rights of women in India.
 
• It reviews laws, policies, and programs affecting women and addresses grievances related to gender discrimination and violence.
 
 
 
• **International Human Rights Commission (IHRC):**
 
 
• A non-governmental organization that works globally to promote human rights awareness and advocacy.
 
• It does not have any legislative or judicial authority to investigate or enforce human rights within sovereign states.

questions.question: At which of the following places was the final match of the T20 Blind Cricket World Cup 2022 held?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**M. Chinnaswamy Stadium, Bengaluru**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The final match of the **T20 Blind Cricket World Cup 2022** was held at the **M. Chinnaswamy Stadium in Bengaluru, India**.
 
• The tournament was organized by the **Cricket Association for the Blind in India (CABI)** under the aegis of the World Blind Cricket Council (WBCC).
 
• India emerged victorious in the final match, showcasing exceptional skills and teamwork to retain their title as champions of blind cricket.
 
• The T20 Blind Cricket World Cup 2022 featured participation from multiple countries, promoting inclusivity and accessibility in sports.
 
• Bengaluru, as the host city, played a pivotal role in providing world-class facilities for the players and organizing a successful event.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Blind Cricket**

 
 
• Blind cricket is a version of cricket adapted for players with visual impairments, governed by the World Blind Cricket Council (WBCC).
 
• The ball used in blind cricket is larger and emits sound to assist players in tracking it.
 
• Players are categorized into three groups based on their visual impairment: B1 (totally blind), B2 (partially blind), and B3 (partially sighted).
 
 
 
• **M. Chinnaswamy Stadium**
 
 
• Located in Bengaluru, Karnataka, it is one of India's premier cricket stadiums and home to the Karnataka State Cricket Association (KSCA).
 
• The stadium has hosted numerous international matches and is also the home ground for the Royal Challengers Bangalore (RCB) in the Indian Premier League (IPL).
 
 
 
• **World Blind Cricket Council (WBCC)**
 
 
• The WBCC is the governing body for blind cricket worldwide, promoting the sport among visually impaired athletes.
 
• It organizes international tournaments, including the T20 Blind Cricket World Cup.
 
 
 
• **Cricket Association for the Blind in India (CABI)**
 
 
• CABI is an independent entity affiliated with the WBCC, responsible for promoting and organizing blind cricket in India.
 
• It plays a critical role in identifying talent and ensuring participation in international tournaments.

questions.question: On Republic Day 2023, which country’s contingent marched alongside the Indian troops?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Egypt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• On Republic Day 2023, Egypt's Armed Forces contingent marched alongside Indian troops as part of the celebrations.
 
• This marked the first time Egypt participated in India's Republic Day parade with a military contingent.
 
• Egyptian President **Abdel Fattah El-Sisi** was the Chief Guest at India's 74th Republic Day celebrations in 2023.
 
• The Egyptian contingent consisted of 144 personnel and symbolized the growing defense ties between India and Egypt.
 
• The participation highlighted the strategic partnership and historical ties between the two nations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **India-Egypt Defense Relations**

 
 
• India and Egypt have strengthened their defense cooperation through joint military exercises and exchanges.
 
• The countries signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on defense cooperation during President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi's visit.
 
• Egypt is seen as a key strategic partner in the Middle East and Africa for India.
 
 
 
• **Republic Day Parade Significance**
 
 
• The Republic Day parade showcases India’s military strength, cultural diversity, and achievements.
 
• It is held annually on January 26th at Rajpath (renamed Kartavya Path) in New Delhi.
 
• The event commemorates the day India’s Constitution came into effect in 1950.
 
 
 
• **Chief Guest Tradition**
 
 
• Inviting a Chief Guest is a tradition to enhance diplomatic ties and signify India's global outreach.
 
• Prominent world leaders have been invited as Chief Guests over the years, including heads of state and government.
 
 
 
• **India-Egypt Historical Ties**
 
 
• India and Egypt share a long-standing friendship dating back to the Non-Aligned Movement era.
 
• Both countries have collaborated in areas like trade, education, and culture, apart from defense.
 
• Egypt was one of the first Arab countries to recognize India's independence in 1947.

questions.question: How many times has the Ganga River been mentioned in the Rigveda?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Ganga River has been mentioned only once in the Rigveda, specifically in Mandala 10, Hymn 75, verse 5.
 
• In the Rigveda, rivers like the Saraswati and Sindhu are more prominently referred to compared to the Ganga.
 
• The mention of the Ganga in the Rigveda is brief, indicating its lesser significance during the early Vedic period compared to later Indian texts.
 
• The Rigveda primarily focuses on the geography of northwest India, which was central to the early Vedic civilization.
 
• Later Vedic texts and epics like the Mahabharata and Ramayana emphasize the spiritual and cultural importance of the Ganga River.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rigveda:** The oldest of the four Vedas, composed around 1500 BCE, it is a collection of hymns dedicated to various deities and natural elements.
 
• **Saraswati River:** Extensively mentioned in the Rigveda, it is described as a mighty and sacred river, often associated with divinity and prosperity.
 
• **Indus River (Sindhu):** The Rigveda highlights the Sindhu River as a major geographical and cultural landmark of the early Vedic civilization.
 
• **Later Vedic Period:** The Ganga gains prominence in later Vedic texts, marking a shift in the geographical focus of Vedic civilization towards eastern India.
 
• **Cultural Significance:** The Ganga River is revered in Hinduism as a sacred entity and is personified as Goddess Ganga in Indian mythology.
